Canadian PM Mark Carney:
At the end of one world order, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk built a secure, sovereign nation guided by his creed: “Peace at home, peace in the world.”
And in this time of rupture, Canada honours that example: strength at home, partnership abroad.
Mr. President, more than 70 years ago, Canada sent maple trees to grow beside and in Anıtkabir as a gesture of peace and friendship between our nations.
Today, those trees stand amongst 48,000 others from over 25 nations.
Today, we planted the seeds of something new: a strategic partnership that will create new opportunities for our workers and our businesses, and greater security and prosperity for both our peoples, and, with our efforts, I believe, for other peoples in this region and more broadly.
With care and commitment, that partnership will grow for generations to come.
